newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Scientists find "new" dinosaur species in Patagonia.
newsitem.headline: Scientists find "new" dinosaur species in Patagonia.

text.p: Argentine paleontologists have discovered two giant dinosaur skeletons of a species never seen before and thought to have lived 115 million years ago, local media reported on Friday.

"They are two skeletons of carnivorous dinosaurs from the late cretaceous period (of the mesozoic era), meaning they are between 110 and 115 million years old," Ruben Cuneo, director of the Paleontology Museum of Trelew, Chubut, told the local DyN news agency.

"Very little is known world-wide about this geological age, and very few remains of dinosaurs from that era have been preserved, especially carnivorous ones," Cuneo said in a separate statement to the Clarin newspaper.
The 30-foot (10-meter)-long skeletons were found in the town of Paso de los Indios in the centre of Chubut province, 800 miles (1,500 km) south of Buenos Aires.
Cuneo said the remains were detected in December and he has worked with a team of 10 scientists since then to prepare the bones for transportation to the museum.
The skeletons were found lying on a rocky surface on the banks of the Chubut river, close to where the remains of a 150-year-old "sauropodous" dinosaur were found last year, Clarin said.
